subject: Nebulous Health - tokens/sec sizing + fallback architecture
messages:
From: Susan Lin <susan@nebuloushealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Initial sizing ask — expected peak profile and SLOs

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier. Attached is a rough usage profile (spreadsheet) but top-level ask below so we can get a preliminary headroom estimate for Dedicated:

- Business context: PBM-style conversational assistant for clinicians. Latency requirements tight for triage flows.
- Traffic profile (expected): peak 1,200 concurrent sessions during daily morning surge (08:00–09:30 PT), sustained for ~90 minutes. Average request = 80 tokens output (response tokens); average prompt size ~40 tokens.
- Peak qps estimate: roughly 200 requests/sec during surge (we measured front-end concurrency -> qps conversion in the sheet). That maps to ~24,000 tokens/sec outgoing (200 * 120 avg total tokens), but some sessions have multi-turns; see sheet.
- SLOs: user-facing p95 latency target = 250ms for single-request flows; acceptable fallback up to 500ms for lower-priority calls.
- Security: data must remain in US region; SOC2 attestation required (we know Redwood supports).

Questions for you: what Dedicated slab would you recommend (GPU type & count) for a baseline commit that meets p95=250ms with 1.5x headroom? Also, what fallback plan (smaller quantized model or degraded path) would you propose?

If you can give a quick ops-level sketch (tokens/sec per GPU for candidate models, buffer factor, recommended commit vs burst limits) that would help us size procurement and internal approval requests.

Attaching: nebula model sheet (very rough).

Thanks,
Susan
Susan Lin
Head of Product, Nebulous Health

Attachment: nebulous_throughput_modeling_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet of traffic samples and conservative multipliers)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask — expected peak profile and SLOs

Hi Susan — quick read of the sheet, thanks. High-level proposal below (ops-friendly bullets) so you can take to procurement/finance:

Summary recommendation (baseline commit + burst):
- Baseline commit: 40 H100 80GB-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool)
- Burst headroom: up to 200 GPUs (on demand) for controlled surges; we can expose a burst bucket with automatic fallback rules
- Hybrid model strategy: run rw-3-70B (full model) for priority flows, and rw-3-13B quantized int8 for lower-tier traffic or degraded fallback.

Throughput math (ballpark):
- rw-3-70B quantized (fast kernels / fused attention): ~520 tokens/sec per H100 for generation at typical 1.5–2ms per token kernel when batched (empirical from similar deals).
- rw-3-13B quantized: ~2,200 tokens/sec per H100 (same kernel set, much smaller memory/KV pressure).

Mapping to your peak:
- Peak outbound tokens/sec (conservative): 30,000 tok/s (I used a 1.25x multiplier on your 24k to account for multi-turns and burstiness).
- If all traffic served on 70B: 30,000 / 520 ≈ 58 GPUs -> round to 65 for p95 buffer (x1.1) + slot fragmentation -> recommend 70 GPUs.
- If we adopt hybrid: keep 30% of requests on 70B and 70% on 13B (for non-critical routings), effective tokens/sec per mixed GPU capacity increases; steady-state GPUs needed ≈ 40 H100 equiv.

Headroom & SLOs:
- To hit p95=250ms we recommend: per-request routing rule that caps 70B concurrency per-instance to maintain stable token latencies.
- Add KV/prefix caching for repeat patterns — that reduces per-request token work by ~12–18% empirically.
- Recommend committed baseline = 40 GPUs (as above) with autoscale to 200; reserve 40-60 GPUs as hot pool for priority lanes. This gives ~1.3–1.8x headroom depending on hybrid split.

Fallback plan (degradation paths):
1) Primary: rw-3-70B (full quality).
2) Fallback A: rw-3-13B quantized — near-instant scale, cheaper token cost, modest quality delta for templates/recurrence flows.
3) Fallback B: throttle + cached response for non-interactive flows (e.g., batchable clinical lookups).

Next steps: ops to validate kernel numbers, and we'll produce a slim SLA fit memo for procurement. Priyom / Karthik — can you sanity-check the per-GPU numbers and give a short ops note on slot fragmentation and canary sizing?

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask — expected peak profile and SLOs

+1 on the hybrid approach. Quick ops notes:

- The 520 tok/s for 70B is a good conservative baseline with our current fused-kernel path; on H100 with 1.2ms steady token kernel we have seen 600–650 tok/s on highly-optimized runs. I kept 520 to be safe for clinical SLOs.
- Fragmentation: pack-based batching will matter — for 200 qps with variable prompt lengths, expect some tail due to uneven batch fill. Add ~10% more GPUs to the math for fragmentation (I recommend adding +10% to Priya's numbers).
- Cold-starts and KV warmup: first-turns cost more. Plan a warmup policy during morning surge (pre-warm top-20 prefixes), reduces token cost by ~15% for those flows.

Attachment: ops_simulation_notes.pdf (short runbook and simulation outputs).

Action items for sizing doc:
- I will run a quick sim using your traffic CSV and return a nominal GPUs-needed curve with different hybrid splits and buffer multipliers. Expect output by EOD.

—Priyom
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Susan Lin <susan@nebuloushealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T14:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask — expected peak profile and SLOs

Susan / team — quick engineering sanity check and additional levers: 

- Quantization profile: INT8 + KV caching + attention-merge reduces memory pressure and gives the 13B path a very favorable cost/throughput. For clinical LLMs where hallucination risk must be low, we can lock generation temperature and add eval gating (adds ~12ms but lowers retries).
- Canary strategy: start with a 10-GPU canary of 13B to validate routing and quality. Once steady, open 70B pool in 2 waves (30 GPUs then ramp) while monitoring p95 and quality regressions on our eval set.
- Autoscale policy: prefer token-budget-based autoscaling (tokens/sec emitted per minute) rather than pure RPS; this matches your workload better.

Numbers (after ops fragmentation + canary buffer):
- All-on-70B conservative: 30,000 tok/s / 520 = 58 -> +10% fragmentation = 64 -> human round-up and safety margin = 75 GPUs.
- Hybrid (30% 70B / 70% 13B): 70B capacity for priority = ~22 GPUs; remaining capacity handled by 13B: (30,000 * 0.7) / 2200 ≈ 10 GPUs -> add fragmentation & safety -> baseline ~40 GPUs total (mix as Priya suggested).

I'll coordinate with infra for quota checks (PGPU IDs) and with product to set the routing rules.

—Karthik

Susan — summary for procurement and execs: clear, numbered items for your packet.

1) Recommended commit (conservative baseline): 40 H100-equivalent GPUs reserved in US region (supports hybrid routing where ~30% priority requests hit 70B).

2) Burst policy: allow autoscale up to 200 GPUs for controlled surges; set automatic fallback to rw-3-13B when 70B pool reaches 85% utilization.

3) Expected cost/throughput tradeoff: hybrid path reduces committed GPU needs from ~75 (all-70B) to ~40 (mixed) with modest quality tradeoffs on low-priority flows. We will provide an SLO memo tying p95 latency windows to routing gates.

4) Operational controls & quality guardrails: KV caching, prefix warmup for top-20 patterns, canary rollout (10 -> 30 GPUs), token-budget autoscaling, rate-limits per-customer route, and an eval gate to catch regressions.

5) Next deliverables (timeline):
   - Ops sim (Priyom): detailed GPU curve by hybrid split (EOD today).
   - SLA fit memo (Priya): 1-pager for procurement (tomorrow).
   - Contract/commit proposal: draft commitment options for 12/24 month terms with burst pricing (sales/finance to coordinate).

Attachments referenced: nebulous_throughput_modeling_v2.xlsx, ops_simulation_notes.pdf

If that looks right I can convert to a short slide + a one-page for procurement. Susan — do you want us to include preliminary pricing tiers tied to committed GPUs or should we wait until sim completes?

Thanks — Priya
